status_legend.supported: A fetched source states the capability exists at the recorded Zed version.
status_legend.absent: A fetched source shows the capability does not exist at the recorded Zed version.
status_legend.unverified: No fetched source states the capability. Never treat this as "no change".

capabilities.evidence: Zed loads project-local skills from <worktree>/.agents/skills/ and global skills from ~/.agents/skills/. Each skill is a direct child of the skills root; nesting is not supported.
capabilities.adapter_use: bin/sync-zed-adapter.sh generates .agents/skills.
capabilities.on_change: If the discovery path or the flat-layout rule changes, update the generator and re-run it.

capabilities.evidence: The documented fields are name (required), description (required; keep under 1024 bytes) and disable-model-invocation (optional). The page still says other Agent Skills fields are planned.
capabilities.adapter_use: The shared export projects every SKILL.md to exactly these three fields.
capabilities.on_change: When Zed honors more fields, widen the projection in bin/_lib-adapter-skills.sh so the dropped fields come back.

capabilities.evidence: A name must use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, must not start or end with a hyphen, must not contain consecutive hyphens, and must be 1-64 characters. Invalid names fail to load and surface an error in the UI.
capabilities.adapter_use: adapter_skill_name_valid() fails generation on a violating folder, and the exporter asserts name matches the folder name.

capabilities.evidence: disable-model-invocation: true hides a skill from the agent's catalog while keeping it invocable via slash command or @-mention.
capabilities.adapter_use: The three approve-* skills keep this field in the generated tree.

capabilities.evidence: A skill can be loaded with a /slash command or an @skill mention, and the agent may invoke it from its catalog. Per-skill permission defaults are available so trusted skills do not prompt.
capabilities.adapter_use: This is how the operator invokes ApexYard skills under Zed.

capabilities.evidence: The total size of all skill names and descriptions is capped at 50KB; skills that do not fit are dropped from the catalog with a warning in the UI.
capabilities.adapter_use: The adapter ships all skills; a growth past the cap would silently drop skills from the catalog.

capabilities.evidence: No fetched source states a hard per-file byte limit. Zed v1.21.0 showed the error "SKILL.md file exceeds maximum size of 100KB" for a 109,268-byte handover SKILL.md (operator report, eibrahim95/apexyard#7). The v1.22.0 skills page documents only conventions: keep the body under 500 lines and the description under 1024 bytes.
capabilities.adapter_use: adapter_skills_export() fails generation when an exported SKILL.md exceeds 100,000 bytes, the smaller reading of 100KB.
capabilities.on_change: When a Zed source states the limit, record it here as supported and set ADAPTER_SKILL_MAX_BYTES in bin/_lib-adapter-skills.sh to match.

capabilities.evidence: Project-local skills load only from trusted worktrees. Skills from a freshly cloned or untrusted project are excluded from the catalog and slash commands until trust is granted.
capabilities.adapter_use: A fresh clone shows no skills until the worktree is trusted.

capabilities.evidence: The skills page states the agent cannot edit SKILL.md files or their bundled resources without explicit authorization, even in a trusted project. Live reload applies to manual changes.
capabilities.adapter_use: Drift in .agents/skills cannot be silently patched in-session; fixes go through bin/sync-zed-adapter.sh regeneration and a PR.

capabilities.evidence: If a global and a project-local skill share the same name, the project-local skill takes precedence.
capabilities.adapter_use: The generated project-local ApexYard skills cannot be shadowed by a same-named global skill.

capabilities.evidence: The skill tool matches patterns against the absolute path to the skill's SKILL.md file, not the skill name, and a user-invoked /skill-name does not prompt again because the skill was explicitly invoked.
capabilities.adapter_use: Documents how to allow or deny individual ApexYard skills.

capabilities.evidence: agent.tool_permissions.default, plus tools.<tool>.{default, always_allow, always_deny, always_confirm} with {pattern, case_sensitive} entries. Tool approval is controlled by agent.tool_permissions.default from v0.224.0 on.
capabilities.adapter_use: bin/install-zed-adapter.sh writes always_deny and always_confirm rules under tools.terminal.
capabilities.on_change: A renamed key silently stops enforcing; re-verify this entry against the live page before changing the installer.

capabilities.evidence: Precedence: built-in security rules, then always_deny, then always_confirm, then always_allow, then the tool default, then the global default.
capabilities.adapter_use: The adapter relies on always_deny outranking a global default of allow.
capabilities.on_change: A weaker deny layer would make the installer rules advisory instead of blocking.

capabilities.evidence: For the terminal tool, Zed parses chained commands (e.g. echo hello && rm file) and checks each sub-command against the patterns, across all supported shells.
capabilities.adapter_use: A deny rule still matches `cd x && git add -A`.

capabilities.evidence: The documented setup paths are the Settings Editor and the user settings file; the installer therefore writes the per-machine user settings file.
capabilities.adapter_use: Every developer runs bin/install-zed-adapter.sh once per machine.

capabilities.evidence: The fetched v1.22.0 page still does not state whether agent.tool_permissions can be set per project. The adapter does not depend on the answer.
capabilities.adapter_use: None. The installer writes user settings.
capabilities.on_change: If a project scope ships, the adapter could generate project rules and drop the per-machine install step.

capabilities.evidence: spawn_agent spawns a subagent with its own context window; each subagent has access to the same tools as the parent agent.
capabilities.adapter_use: Review skills are told to spawn the reviewer with spawn_agent and a prompt that adopts the reviewer agent-definition file.
capabilities.on_change: If Zed ships typed subagents with restricted tools, the reviewer read-only gap closes.

capabilities.evidence: The tools page states a subagent gets the parent's tools. No read-only subagent tier is documented.
capabilities.adapter_use: The reviewer read-only rule stays advisory; the spawn prompt must instruct the subagent not to modify the repository.

capabilities.evidence: The v1.22.0 release notes list an optional model parameter for spawn_agent to choose a model for that spawn instead of using the configured subagent model or inheriting the parent model (zed-industries/zed#64498). The same release enabled compaction for subagents (zed-industries/zed#64135).
capabilities.adapter_use: Reviewer spawn prompts may pin a smaller or cheaper model for read-only review passes; no gate changes.

capabilities.evidence: No fetched page documents project files that define agent personas or per-agent model/tool configuration for the native agent.
capabilities.adapter_use: The adapter generates no agent files; reviewer personas travel in the spawn prompt.

capabilities.evidence: The hooks documentation page returns 404 at v1.22.0, and no fetched page documents an agent.hooks setting. The proposal zed-industries/zed#57890 (closed 2026-05-28, state_reason completed) covered commands, lifecycle hooks and skills together; only skills are documented today.
capabilities.adapter_use: None. Every blocking gate except the tool-permission rules is advisory under the native agent.
capabilities.on_change: Add a hooks transport that delegates to the unmodified .claude/hooks/*.sh scripts, and re-tier the adapter.

capabilities.evidence: External agents integrate over ACP and are installed from the ACP Registry; Claude Agent is registered there and may read CLAUDE.md directly.
capabilities.adapter_use: Documents the second Zed path: run Claude Code over ACP and keep the full .claude/ enforcement layer.

capabilities.evidence: The External Agents page states Zed Skills do not apply as Zed Skills in External Agent threads; the agent's native skills and instructions depend on the agent.
capabilities.adapter_use: Under the ACP path the .agents/skills export is not used; Claude Agent reads .claude/ itself.

capabilities.evidence: The tools page references a separate Agent Sandboxing page for OS-level restrictions on the terminal tool. A fetch of https://zed.dev/docs/ai/agent-sandboxing returned 404 at Zed v1.22.0 (2026-10-04); the live page was not located this run.
capabilities.adapter_use: None. The adapter does not depend on sandboxing.
capabilities.on_change: Read the Agent Sandboxing page before relying on sandboxing as a gate.
